To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
co operative banks are more stable and less risky than commercial banks, but they are less profitable, and their efficiency is not significantly higher than that of the joint stock banks.
co operative banks perform well in terms of financial stability and social responsibility and that they can improve their performance further by increasing their degree of strategic integration.

co operative banking networks are a viable business model, with a performance that is at least as good as that of their joint stock bank competitors, and that they have a strong future, with a number of advantages that are likely to strengthen their position in the market.

the performance of the co operative sector and its ability to compete in a highly competitive environment, where commercial banks are increasingly adopting co operative values and practices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
co operative banks have performed better than their commercial joint stock counterparts over the period 2005–16 in the European Union and in the United Kingdom.
co operative banking networks are performing well in Europe.

, in the European context at least, there is no single model of co operative banking that can be considered superior to all others, but rather the model that is best for a particular co operative bank is one that best suits its own specific circumstances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

co operative banking is alive and well, and that co operative banks are performing as well or better than commercial joint stock banks, with the best performers being the most strategically integrated co operative banking networks.
the co operative banking sector has been performing better than its commercial joint stock counterparts, but the performance gap has been narrowing.
the co operative banking networks in Europe are a success story, and they have been for a very long time.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite the challenges they face, European co operative banks continue to perform better than their commercial counterparts, especially in terms of their contribution to economic and social development.
, in general, co operative banks perform better than commercial banks.
co operative banking networks have been able to deliver superior performance over time compared with commercial joint stock banks.
